editorial.headline: Public Relations: Nationally Open, but No PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A public-relations activity open to 100% foreign ownership nationally, but unavailable to PT PMA registration in Bali today.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor, the decisive fact is Balinese: a PT PMA cannot register this activity in Bali today. That local outcome sits beside a nationally open classification, so this is not a universally closed activity. The distinction matters because the stated national ownership ceiling and the local registration result point in different directions.

The activity itself is public-relations work in the practical sense. It covers advice, guidance and operational assistance given to companies and other organisations on public relations and communications. It also covers lobbying, together with sales-representation activity undertaken for promotional purposes. Read as a whole, the scope describes a communications-facing service that can combine counsel with hands-on support and promotional representation. It is work concerned with the relationship between an organisation, its communications, and its external representation. It is not merely a title for public messaging: the recorded scope deliberately reaches operational assistance as well as advice.

At the national level, the PMA status is **TERBUKA**, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. The registration scales listed for the activity are Mikro, Kecil and Menengah. Those two facts need to be read together without smoothing away the distinction: the national investment setting is open, while the available scale rows named in the record stop at Menengah. The record names no Usaha Besar row among those listed scales, and supplies no further conditions for this activity.

Bali changes the practical conclusion. Its stated status is **CHIUSO_PMA_NO_BESAR**: OSS has no Usaha Besar scale row, the activity is reserved for UMKM, and a PT PMA—Usaha Besar by law—cannot register it. This is the structural reason given in the record, rather than a qualification to the national ownership ceiling. In addition, the province has a permanent, island-wide rule blocking PMA registration for activities classed as Low or Medium-Low risk. Neither the national 100% ceiling nor the open national status creates a Bali registration path for a PT PMA under the recorded position. Founders should therefore treat the national and Bali readings as distinct: open nationally, but closed to PMA registration in Bali today.
